stem: A disease that spreads across many countries and continents is described as

options.rationale: Correct: pan means all or across.
Endemic means always present in one area.
Chronic means long-lasting, usually not infectious.
Hereditary means passed on through genes.

explanation: A pandemic is an epidemic that spreads across many countries and continents.

options.rationale: Correct: cholera bacteria come from human waste.
Mosquitoes spread malaria, not cholera.

options.content: eating too much sugar and salt

stem: Malaria is always present at a steady level in some low-lying parts of Zimbabwe. This means malaria is ___ there.

options.rationale: A pandemic spreads across many countries at once.
Eradicated would mean it no longer exists.
An epidemic is a sudden rise above the normal level.
Correct: always present in an area.

explanation: Endemic diseases are constantly present in a particular area.

stem: Which of these is a way that HIV can be passed on?

options.content: hugging a person living with HIV
options.rationale: HIV is not spread by hugging.
HIV is not spread by sharing plates.
Mosquitoes do not spread HIV.
Correct: infected blood can pass on HIV.

explanation: HIV spreads through unprotected sex, infected blood (shared sharp instruments) and from mother to child, not by everyday contact.

stem: In which year did Zimbabwe record its first case of COVID-19?

options.rationale: Cyclone Idai struck in 2019.
2008 is remembered for the start of a major cholera outbreak.
Correct: the first case was recorded in March 2020.
2016 is not linked to COVID-19.

explanation: COVID-19 reached Zimbabwe in March 2020, the same month WHO declared a pandemic.

stem: During a cholera outbreak, a council trucks safe water into a suburb and repairs burst sewers. Why are these actions more important than medicine alone?

options.content: Cholera cannot be treated by any medicine
options.rationale: Cholera can be treated, e.g. with oral rehydration.

options.content: They remove the source of infection, so new cases stop
options.rationale: Correct: cholera spreads through unsafe water and sanitation.

options.content: Safe water cures people who are already sick
options.rationale: Treatment at a clinic is still needed for the sick.

options.content: Sewers spread the disease through the air
options.rationale: Cholera is not airborne.

explanation: Treatment saves the sick, but only safe water and sanitation stop new infections.
hints: Medicine treats the sick; what prevents new infections?

stem: Tatenda fears being rejected and so refuses to be tested for HIV. Which problem does this show?

options.content: testing for HIV is banned in Zimbabwe
options.rationale: Testing is widely available.

options.content: HIV cannot be detected by any test
options.rationale: HIV tests are reliable.
Correct: fear of rejection keeps people from testing.

options.content: treatment works only for people who never test
options.rationale: Treatment depends on knowing one's status.

explanation: Stigma makes people hide symptoms and avoid testing, which harms them and helps disease spread.
hints: Why might a person hide or avoid finding out?

stem: Which statement **best** evaluates the COVID-19 lockdowns in Zimbabwe?

options.content: They had no effect on the spread of the disease at all
options.rationale: Restricting contact does slow spread.

options.content: They benefited every family equally and caused no hardship to anyone at all
options.rationale: Many families lost income.

options.content: They slowed the spread but caused hardship for informal traders
options.rationale: Correct: a balanced judgement of benefit and cost.

options.content: They ended the pandemic in Zimbabwe within one week
options.rationale: The pandemic lasted much longer.

explanation: Lockdowns reduced contact and slowed spread, but families who depend on daily informal trade lost income.
hints: An evaluation gives both a benefit and a cost.

stem: There is a cure for HIV.
explanation: False. There is no cure, but antiretroviral therapy taken as prescribed lets people living with HIV lead long, healthy lives.

stem: Washing hands with soap helps prevent the spread of cholera, dysentery and COVID-19.
explanation: True. Hand washing removes germs that spread through contaminated hands.

stem: Match each disease with its main way of spreading.

right.content: contact with the body fluids of a sick person
unprotected sex, infected blood, mother to child
water or food contaminated with faeces
droplets and particles in the air

explanation: Each disease spreads in a different way, so each needs different prevention.

payload.template: The treatment that allows people living with HIV to live long, healthy lives is called {{blank:a}}. A sudden large outbreak in one country is called {{blank:b}}.

explanation: ART controls HIV; a sudden large outbreak in one area is an epidemic.

stem: Distinguish between endemic, epidemic and pandemic.

points.description: Endemic: always present in an area at a steady level
Epidemic: a sudden rise in cases in one community, country or region
Pandemic: spreads across many countries and continents

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: An endemic disease is always present in an area, such as malaria in some low-lying parts of Zimbabwe. An epidemic is a sudden rise in cases in one area, such as the cholera outbreak of 2008-2009. A pandemic spreads across many countries and continents, such as COVID-19.

explanation: One mark for each correct meaning.

stem: Explain **three** economic effects of a pandemic such as COVID-19 on Zimbabwe.

points.description: Identifies loss of income for informal traders/workers
Develops: lockdowns stopped trading, so families could not buy food
Identifies business closures / job losses / fall in tourism
Develops: businesses lost customers and laid off workers; tourists stopped coming
Identifies higher government spending on health / less for development
Develops: money went to testing, treatment and vaccines instead of roads or schools

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Informal traders could not trade during lockdowns, so many families lost their daily income and struggled to buy food. Businesses lost customers and some closed or laid off workers, and tourism collapsed when borders closed. The government had to spend heavily on testing, treatment and vaccines, leaving less money for other development.

explanation: One mark for each effect and one for its development.
hints: Think of households, businesses and the government.

stem: Suggest **two** ways a school could reduce the spread of infectious diseases among its learners, and explain how each would help.

points.description: Suggests hand-washing points with soap and water / clean toilets
Explains that germs from hands or faeces are removed, reducing cholera, dysentery and respiratory infections
Suggests health education / sick learners stay home / ventilated classrooms / supporting vaccination campaigns
Explains how it reduces contact with germs or builds knowledge

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The school could put hand-washing points with soap outside the toilets and dining hall, which removes germs and reduces diarrhoeal diseases. It could also keep classroom windows open and ask learners with a cough or fever to stay home, which reduces the spread of diseases through the air.

explanation: One mark for each suitable measure and one for its explanation.

stem:
**Source A** — a poster of the kind used in a public health campaign (described in words) (described in words; invented for this question)

> The poster shows a tap with a bar of soap beside it, a covered water container and a clean toilet. Large words read: "Clean hands, safe water, clean toilets: stop cholera." Underneath, smaller words say: "Diarrhoea? Drink oral rehydration solution and go to the clinic at once."

Study Source A and answer the questions.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which disease is the poster mainly about?

options.rationale: HIV is not spread by dirty water.
Correct: the poster names cholera.
Diabetes is not infectious.
The poster's focus is water and sanitation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Identify **two** prevention measures shown on the poster.

points.description: Hand washing with soap
Safe (covered) water / using clean toilets

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Washing hands with soap and keeping drinking water covered and safe (also clean toilets).

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain why the poster tells people with diarrhoea to go to the clinic at once.

points.description: Cholera causes severe watery diarrhoea
The body loses water quickly (dehydration), which can kill within hours
Trained health workers can give rehydration and treatment / record and contain the outbreak

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Cholera causes severe watery diarrhoea, so the body loses water very quickly and a person can die from dehydration within hours. At the clinic, trained health workers can give rehydration and treatment and report the case so the outbreak can be contained.

explanation: A source-based practice item on preventing and responding to cholera.
hints: In (c), think about how fast cholera can harm the body.

stem: This question is about HIV and AIDS.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Describe **two** social effects of HIV and AIDS on families and communities.

points.description: Effect 1, e.g. orphans / child-headed households
Described: e.g. children care for siblings and may leave school
Effect 2, e.g. stigma / burden of care / loss of breadwinners
Described: e.g. people rejected or hide status; relatives spend time and money caring for the sick

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Many children lost parents to AIDS, and some households came to be headed by children, who cared for younger siblings and sometimes left school. Stigma led some people living with HIV to be rejected, so others hid their status and avoided testing.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Evaluate the measures used to fight HIV and AIDS in Zimbabwe.

points.description: Testing and ART: people live long, healthy lives; treatment also reduces transmission; limits: daily lifelong treatment, supply, stigma
Prevention education and condoms/prevention of mother-to-child transmission: strengths and limits (behaviour change is slow)
Funding and coordination (AIDS levy, National AIDS Council, partners): strengths and limits (dependence on donors)
Supported overall judgement

levels.descriptor: Developed explanation of several relevant points or arguments, supported by accurate, specific knowledge and examples, considering more than one side and reaching a supported judgement that answers the question.
Developed explanation of some factors or arguments with relevant supporting detail; a judgement is attempted but is only partly supported, or the other side is thin.
Some explanation of one or two relevant factors, or several points described with limited explanation; little or no judgement.
Simple, general or narrative statements with limited relevance to the question; little explanation.

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
Testing and antiretroviral therapy have been the most important measures. People who know their status and take ART every day can lead long, healthy lives, and effective treatment also greatly reduces the chance of passing HIV on. However, treatment must be taken for life, supplies must never run out, and stigma still keeps some people from testing.

Prevention education in schools, churches and the media, condoms, and programmes to prevent mother-to-child transmission have helped many people protect themselves and their babies. Changing behaviour is slow, though, and myths still circulate.

The response is funded partly through the AIDS levy and coordinated by the National AIDS Council with partners such as the Global Fund. This shows national commitment, but much of the money still comes from outside partners, which is a risk if support falls.

Overall, these measures have been largely successful in turning HIV from a death sentence into a manageable condition, but the fight is not over while stigma remains and new infections continue.

explanation: A practice evaluative item on the response to HIV and AIDS.
hints: In (b), give a strength and a limit of each measure, then judge.
